construct: The Z alpha-1 antitrypsin variant misfolds and polymerizes within hepatocyte endoplasmic reticulum, causing toxic intracellular accumulation and liver disease. Reduced secretion simultaneously lowers circulating AAT, permitting neutrophil-elastase-mediated alveolar destruction in the lung.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: PI*ZZ with basilar panacinar emphysema and PAS-positive diastase-resistant hepatocyte globules identifies AAT deficiency; liver injury comes from toxic ER retention/polymerization of misfolded Z-AAT, while lung injury reflects loss of antiprotease function.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Neutrophil elastase is the lung mechanism, not the hepatic one. Wilson disease, mitochondrial beta-oxidation defects, and autoantibody mechanisms do not explain PI*ZZ PAS-positive diastase-resistant ER inclusions.
